A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references and Appendices A–E. All substantive material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Transformer prediction, solver-runtime and generalization experiments in Section 5, plus sampling, embedding and computational analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the runtime comparisons, cumulative-polynomial-product experiments and additional appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The oracle-guided border basis algorithm, oracle-call cap and fallback, sampling procedures, monomial embedding and fast Gaussian elimination kernel are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic polynomial systems over F7, F31 and F127, higher-degree generalization scenarios and cumulative-polynomial-product task. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The BBA, IBBA and FGE comparison sets in Tables 2 and 6–8 are unchanged. Infix tokenization remains the comparator for monomial embedding in Table 3.

E3.justification: Training and evaluation sample counts, model settings, training budgets, truncation levels, metrics, oracle-call budgets and border-gap thresholds match in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

E4.justification: Both retain the same truncation and embedding comparisons, backward-transform validation, out-of-distribution tests, runtime-bottleneck analysis and border-gap studies. No ablation or supplementary analysis changes.

E5.justification: Both report mean and standard deviation over 100 random systems for runtime comparisons, the same zero-reduction variability reporting, and the same quartile/whisker plots. No repetition, seed or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted findings and qualitative results match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, both versions' Table 2 reports 7.60 seconds for IBBA and 2.58 seconds for OBBA in the F31, n = 5 row.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems and proofs are retained, including correctness and cost analysis in Appendix A, sampling theory in Appendix B and the generator-transform proof in Appendix C.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims of correctness-preserving acceleration, a border-basis sampling theorem, efficient monomial representation and speedups up to 3.5 times.

C2.justification: Explanations of the computational bottleneck, embedding benefits and generalization remain unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning zero-dimensional ideals and experiments restricted to finite fields with up to five variables.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, polynomial sampling instructions, hardware and training-time disclosures in Appendices D–E are unchanged. The code-access statement and repository URL are also retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Reference [19] changes 'Gruel' to 'Greuel' and 'Sringer' to 'Springer', which are bibliographic spelling corrections rather than a different citation.

P1.justification: Several appendix pointers now say 'Section' or 'Sections'; reference [19] has spelling corrections, and the version/date stamp is updated. Structure and substantive prose remain intact. The Section 3.2 hyperlink labeled Theorem A.5 now incorrectly targets Theorem 4.5.

P2.justification: There is limited paragraph reflow and spacing adjustment, plus repositioning of the first-page version/date stamp. Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–9 retain their content, captions, organization and placement.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical support and reproducibility information remain unchanged. Reference [19] receives small editorial corrections, while the misdirected Theorem A.5 hyperlink introduces a small navigation regression. These limited presentation changes do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
